title: curated-econ-simulator-and-drift-aware-batcher-presets
author: Priya Sharma
description:
Motivation: teams repeatedly ask for better defaults that balance latency and unit economics without manual tuning. This PR introduces a lightweight 'Econ Curator' service plus a drift-aware presets layer for the batcher and cache defaults. The goal is twofold: 1) provide curated batching/caching/quantization presets tailored to common workload archetypes, 2) surface a fast simulation tool that projects unit-econ impact of profile changes so platform and product engineers can make informed rollouts.

What this changes (high level): adds a small simulation CLI and HTTP shim (optimize/econ_simulator) that replays representative traces against candidate presets, computes per-token cost, tail-latency, and expected throughput; implements a curator that synthesizes presets from historical telemetry and workload labels; adds drift detection hooks that mark presets as stale when request distributions shift; wires presets into the batcher defaults with safe fallback logic; ships a set of canonical quantization profiles (fp16/int8/4bit mixed) that are benchmarked against targeted context lengths.

Why this is safe: defaults are gated behind a feature flag (optimize.curator.enabled=false) and rollout uses canary policy (10% -> 50% -> 100%). The batcher integration includes an automatic fallback to current pinned presets if the simulator reports regressions above configured thresholds. No schema changes to persisted model configs; all new state is stored under a namespaced key in the existing Optimize configstore so upgrades are backwards compatible.

Included artifacts: curated preset JSONs for three archetypes (low-latency chat, high-throughput embedding, mixed interactive inference); a small Go shim for realtime lookups (redwood/serve/batcher/presets.go); a Python simulator that can run locally or in CI (redwood/optimize/econ_simulator/sim.py); unit economics calculators embedded in the Optimize UI backend (redwood/optimize/api/econ.py); integration tests that exercise preset rollouts and simulator assertions.

Testing & CI: unit tests for curator logic, simulator determinism tests using recorded traces, integration tests for batcher fallback and canary rollouts. One flaky integration test (simulator/replay/latency_match) failed on the first run due to an ordering race; I added a deterministic seed and a retry in the test harness and reran CI. All checks are green.

Migration and rollout notes: default is off; to enable at org-level set optimize.curator.enabled=true and configure optimize.curator.canary_fraction. Operators can run the simulator locally against a saved trace (scripts/run_sim.sh) to preview cost delta. Release notes: introduces Econ Curator and drift-aware batcher presets; opt-in behind feature flag; no breaking changes.

Checklist (brief): - [x] curator core synthesis algorithm + unit tests - [x] simulator + deterministic trace runner - [x] batcher presets hook + safe fallback - [x] QA integration tests and e2e smoke - [x] docs (Optimize docs + quickstart)

Related work: references ENG-2207 (cost automation initiative) and ENG-2224 (batcher rewrite for presets).

review_comments: Evan Martin: Nice overall shape. Two asks: (1) can we expose a per-org opt-in toggle in the console UI rather than only via helm/values, (2) I worry about default thresholds for fallback—please document the rationale and make them configurable.

Priya Sharma: Added console toggle wiring in console/ui components and documented the rationale + made thresholds configurable via optimize.curator.thresholds in helm values. Responded with unit tests validating threshold overrides.

Sofia Alvarez: Simulator looks great, but can we add a short-circuit that avoids expensive replay when the trace size is above the configured limit? This is important for on-prem environments with limited CI budgets.
Priya Sharma: Added a fast-sample mode and a 'max_trace_events' config. CI uses sampled traces by default; full replays are still available via the CLI. Added tests to assert sampler correctness.
Marcus Chen: Approve after small nits: bump gofmt on presets.go and add comment on fallback invariants.
Priya Sharma: Addressed gofmt and added comments per request. Thanks!
ci_logs_summary: CI pipeline: lint -> unit -> integration -> e2e
Initial integration run: 1 failing test (simulator/replay/latency_match) due to nondeterministic seed
Fix: deterministic seed + test retry added in f0a1c6e
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash after approvals from reviewers. Feature gated and disabled by default.
release_notes: Add Econ Curator service and drift-aware batcher presets. Ships behind feature flag optimize.curator.enabled=false. Introduces simulator CLI for cost projection and canonical quantization profiles. Opt-in; no breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: To enable at org scale: set optimize.curator.enabled=true and configure optimize.curator.canary_fraction and optimize.curator.thresholds in values.optimize.yaml. Run tools/run_sim.sh with a representative trace to preview unit-econ impact. Monitor optimize.econ.simulation.* metrics and canary rollout alerts.
